notes:
CIRCUIT: a 3-rail x 5-column ladder/grid. Three horizontal rails (top y~292, middle y~468, bottom y~610) are each interrupted by two series parts, and five vertical columns (x~105, 315, 478, 670, 840) each carry one diode/zener between the top and middle rails and one more between the middle and bottom rails. A 4th, plain rail at y~700 carries the GND symbol and closes the loop from the far-left drop (x~32) round to the 2kOhm resistor on the far right. 18 components, 9 nets.

NET MAP (each rail is cut into segments by the series parts sitting in it, so a rail is NOT one node):
  0  (GND) = middle-rail segment A, x~32 to x~394, i.e. from the left end of the middle rail east past the x~105 column (S16) and the x~315 column (S17) to the LEFT plate of the 1uF cap #7; PLUS the far-left drop that leaves the middle rail at (32,466), runs down to (43,700) and becomes the bottom-most rail y~700, which runs east to (905,697); PLUS the GND stub at (519,705) (S45); PLUS the bottom lead of the 2kOhm resistor #13 at (924,595) which comes down to (905,697). Terminals: 2.1 (V-DC bottom), 3.0 (zener #3 bottom), 7.0 (cap #7 left), 9.0 (I-DC top), 13.1 (2k resistor bottom), 14.1 (diode #14 top), 17.0 (GND). 7 terminals.
  n1 = top-rail segment 2, x~269 to x~553: right lead of the 1uH inductor #1, east past the x~315 column top (S0) and the x~490 column top (S1), to the LEFT plate of the 1uF cap #0. Terminals 0.0, 1.1, 3.1, 4.1.
  n2 = top-rail segment 3, x~591 to the top-right corner x~850: right plate of cap #0, east past the x~677 column top (S3) to x~848 where it drops onto diode #6. Terminals 0.1, 5.1, 6.0.
  n3 = top-rail segment 1, x~110 to x~180: top-left corner down the x~110 stub to the TOP terminal of the 5V source #2. Terminals 1.0, 2.0.
  n4 = middle-rail segment B, x~430 to x~700: right plate of cap #7 east past the x~478 column (S18) and the x~670 column (S19) to the LEFT lead of the 1uH inductor #8. Terminals 4.0, 5.0, 7.1, 8.0, 10.1, 12.1. 6 terminals - the busiest node.
  n5 = middle-rail segment C, x~781 to x~925: right lead of inductor #8 east past the x~840 column (S20) to the right end, then down to the TOP of the 2kOhm resistor #13. Terminals 6.1, 8.1, 11.1, 13.0.
  n6 = bottom-rail segment 1, x~95 to x~168: bottom terminal of the 1A current source #9 down to (95,605) then east to the LEFT plate of the 1uF cap #15. Terminals 9.1, 15.1.

  n8 = bottom-rail segment 2, x~206 to x~523: right plate of cap #15 east past the x~305 column (S33) and the x~470 column (S34) to the LEFT lead of inductor #16. Terminals 12.0, 14.0, 15.0, 16.0.

CRITICAL SITE DECISIONS - all eleven read JUNCTION. Detail:
  S1 (492,293) deg3 and S3 (676,301) deg3: plain T's, the column ENDS on the top rail. No crossing available.
  S33 (306,607), S34 (464,613), S35 (659,614) deg3: plain T's, the column ENDS on the bottom rail. No crossing available.
  S45 (520,697) deg4: the GND symbol's stub meets the bottom-most rail; GND is net 0 by rule.
  S16 (104,462), S17 (314,466), S18 (477,471), S19 (674,476), S20 (838,479) are the five deg4 rail-crosses-column sites and are the only real judgement calls on this sheet. All five are plain X's: no solder dot (dot metric 1.6-2.2, i.e. barely above stroke width, and nothing symmetric in both axes) and no semicircular hop or sideways jog. I dumped the pixels at the three with the largest 'hop' score - S20 (hop 4.2), S19 (hop 3.6) and S16 (hop 2.1) - with inkmap.py at win=20: in each case the column ink runs straight into the rail ink and out the other side as a single solid overlap; the 'hop' score is just the drafter's slow leftward drift in a long freehand vertical (about 4 px over 40 px of run), not a detour around the rail. I therefore read all five as JUNCTION.
    Consequence of the other reading, e.g. at S20: 'crossing' would split n5 into (rail-west + inductor #8 right) and (rail-east + 2kOhm top) and would put diode #6's bottom and diode #11's top on their own private 2-terminal net. That is not electrically impossible, so the decision rests on the ink prior stated in the brief (in this dataset a hop or jog is drawn when 'not connected' is meant, so a plain crossing is a junction) plus the drafter's own habit on this sheet: this sheet contains no hop and no jog anywhere, and the grid is clearly meant as a ladder in which each column is a rung between the rails. Reading any of the five as a crossing would also leave that column's two diodes in a series pair with no third connection, which is a pointless branch to draw. Same argument applies verbatim to S16, S17, S18, S19.
    S16 additionally would, under the 'crossing' reading, put the 5V source's bottom and the 1A source's top on an isolated 2-terminal net, cutting both sources out of the circuit entirely - the closest thing to an electrical impossibility among the five, and it decides S16 outright.

NON-CRITICAL sites (all left at the default junction) are handwritten value glyphs touching wire or symbol ink: S5,S7,S8 and S27,S37,S40 ('1uH' under the three inductors); S11,S12,S14,S15 and S22,S23 and S38,S42,S43 ('1uF' under the three capacitors); S29 ('1A' beside the current source); S0 is a genuine T (top rail meets the x~315 column) but was not flagged critical because the zener above it was mis-ported at the time - it is a junction and is now load-bearing for n1.

  comp #3 (5V zener, top-left column): t1 was p2@(362,366), a stroke of the '5v' glyph to the right (run 10 px). Remapped t1 -> p1@(326,337), the real top lead (run 41 px, reaching the top rail).
  comp #7 (1uF cap, middle rail): t1 was p3@(410,498), a stroke of the '1uF' glyph below (run 9 px). Remapped t1 -> p1@(430,472), the real right plate lead (run 45 px).
  comp #12 (5V zener, x~470 column below the middle rail): t1 was p2@(505,546), a stroke of the '5v' glyph (run 19 px). Remapped t1 -> p0@(473,517), the real top lead (run 44 px, reaching the middle rail). Note p0 and p1 both report run=44 - that is the run LENGTH, not an id; the two leads are genuinely 44 px each and land on different nets (n4 above, n8 below), so the zener is not shorted.

  comp #9 (1A I-DC) needed no port change - both its leads were already correct; its one-terminal net n9 was a symptom of comp #15's error, not its own.

CLASSES: verified all 18 in the comps montages. The three symbols annotated 'Zener Diode' (#3, #5, #12) are exactly the three whose bar is drawn with the Z-shaped end flicks and which carry a '5v' label; the five annotated 'Diode' (#4, #6, #10, #11, #14) have a plain straight bar and no label. #2 is a circled +/- (V-DC), #9 is a circled arrow (I-DC), #1/#8/#16 are coils, #0/#7/#15 are two-plate caps, #13 is a zig-zag with '2kOhm', #17 is the three-bar ground. No reclassification.

SANITY CHECK ON THE LEFT AND RIGHT RETURN PATHS (both verified at 5x zoom): the middle rail really does continue west past the x~105 column to x~32, turn down and become the y~700 rail, so the middle rail's LEFT segment is ground; and the 2kOhm's bottom lead really does reach that same y~700 rail at (905,697). The bottom rail (y~610) does NOT continue down to y~700 at either end - its right end stops at the (823,605) corner - so the 2kOhm is across n5-to-ground and is not shorted out.

UNRESOLVED: nothing. All 35 terminals have nets, every net has >=2 terminals, ERC clean.
